assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength optical lattice proposal and Ye's demonstrations of clocks reaching 10^-18 uncertainty are a clear, original idea turned into a transformative instrument. The impact is lasting: a redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the lattice clock; Ye led its realisation at ultimate precision, with a very clean two-person configuration. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Katori and Ye collaborators) contributed but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many laboratories worldwide; the technology is mature and in use in metrology institutes. Timing is good, though the formal redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Whether the redefinition of the second has yet occurred is not something I can confirm.
Relative weight of Katori's proposal versus Ye's precision demonstrations may be debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Car-Parrinello method unified electronic-structure theory and molecular dynamics and opened first-principles simulation of liquids, interfaces and materials. As a computational physicist with a stake in simulation methods, I judge its lasting impact to be enormous and its originality clear.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper has exactly two authors, giving a natural and unambiguous two-person prize. The credited names fully capture the decisive contribution.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and independent validation; entirely mature, if arguably overdue. The main concern is whether a method is considered physics rather than chemistry.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views a computational method as a physics discovery or invention.
Some related work (Kohn-Sham, 2013 chemistry prize for multiscale models) overlaps adjacent recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type many-body models with tunable parameters, giving quantum simulators of strongly correlated matter. This connects directly to statistical-physics questions of phases, transitions and dynamics. Originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and others) supplied the theoretical proposal for the Bose-Hubbard realisation; Greiner and Bloch realised the Mott insulator transition (with Hansch and Esslinger in the broader story). Esslinger's fermionic work is also decisive, so a three-person selection necessarily leaves out a key contributor.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many groups, and quantum gas microscopes have extended the field. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller is contentious and limited to three.
Overlap with the Bose-Einstein condensation prize of 2001 and potential overlap with quantum-simulation credit in other candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele proposal of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification, plus the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, opened the field of topological insulators. The conceptual shift is deep and the impact is lasting across condensed matter and materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the theoretical founders; Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental realisation (with theory by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang). The omission of Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes is a real attribution complication, and other candidates split the topic.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many materials, though applications remain limited. Recognition would be timely and arguably overdue after the 2016 topological-phase prize.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) lies outside the supplied names.
Overlap with the other topological insulator candidate on this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Vicsek model, Toner-Tu hydrodynamic theory and the Ramaswamy active-matter formulation established that nonequilibrium collective motion breaks the Mermin-Wagner expectations and forms a new universality class. This is a core statistical-physics advance with broad reach to biology and soft matter, and I regard it as important.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek introduced the minimal model, Toner and Tu the continuum theory with long-range order in two dimensions, and Ramaswamy the hydrodynamics of active fluids. All three are plausible; Marchetti, Tu and others are also strongly associated with the field.
assessment.maturity: Experimental support from bacterial suspensions, colloidal swimmers and flocks is substantial but quantitative tests of exponents remain partial. Probably slightly early but maturing quickly.
uncertainties: Quantitative experimental verification of the Toner-Tu exponents is limited.
Credit is spread over many contributors, so a three-person cut is somewhat arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 launched quantum cryptography and secure communication whose security is guaranteed by physical law. The idea is original and has driven quantum information science, with practical networks and satellites now exist.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard are the unambiguous originators of BB84; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is an independent contribution, so a two-person prize is cleaner but leaves a notable omission.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are mature and deployed, though the 2022 prize to Aspect, Clauser and Zeilinger recognised the entanglement foundation, which could be seen as already covering part of this territory.
uncertainties: Ekert's credit relative to BB84 may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KPZ equation is a paradigm of nonequilibrium statistical physics, linking stochastic growth to random matrices through Tracy-Widom statistics. My own research touches stochastic processes and random matrices, so I know the depth of this connection. The originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: KPZ (1986) is by Kardar, Parisi and Zhang; Parisi is not supplied here and has already won in 2021. Spohn is credited for exact mathematical results, but the physical origin lies with Kardar and Zhang. The configuration is somewhat awkward because of Parisi's absence.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation of exponents and Tracy-Widom statistics in liquid-crystal turbulence (Takeuchi and Sano) and other systems is strong, and mathematical proofs are available. Mature, with maybe not much practical impact.
uncertainties: Parisi's omission from the credited names and the prior prize complicate a fair configuration.
Impact is mostly conceptual with limited technological consequence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser was a genuinely new design principle based on intersubband transitions in engineered heterostructures, and it opened mid-infrared and terahertz sources used for sensing and spectroscopy. The invention is original with lasting practical impact.
assessment.attribution: Faist, Capasso and Cho (with Sirtori, Sivco and Hutchinson) built the first device at Bell Labs in 1994; Capasso led the group, Faist did the first demonstration, and Cho provided molecular-beam epitaxy. The three-person cut leaves out other Bell Labs co-authors.
assessment.maturity: Commercially deployed and reproduced worldwide; fully mature. Timing is fine.
uncertainties: Internal Bell Labs allocation of credit between Capasso, Faist and Cho is unclear to me.
Possible perception that the work is more engineering than physics.
